newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks ride U.S. roller coaster.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks ride U.S. roller coaster.

text.p: South African shares rode a United States-inspired roller coaster on Friday and ended firmly down after taking a knock from Thursday's huge fall on Wall Street, dealers said.
Dow Jones industrial shares shed 160 points in the fifth biggest points fall ever and the reaction was immediate upon South African shares as they tumbled.
The drop had been triggered by a sudden bout of panic on the outlook for short-term U.S. interest rates, with many fearing an imminent hike.
However, just before the close of trade figures were released that showed U.S producer prices had fallen by more than expected, doing much to soothe market fears.
South African stocks took heart and launched a late rally that saw them recapture some of the earlier lost ground.
The all-share index dropped 44.5 points to 7,127.1 as industrials shed 46.9 points to end at 8,327.2.
South African shares were particularly vulnerable to international influences as investors, saturated with local facts and figures from the recent budget, looked abroad for future guidance.
The trend is set to continue next week with all eyes firmly fixed on New York.
The golds index had another weak day as more bullion price fears plagued the market. The index ended off 21.3 points, or 1.49 percent, to 1,408.3.
